cues.en: You may have heard that deep learning requires a very large number of samples in order to train the models, so we need to have a lot of data to fit these models.
cues.zh: 你可能聽過，深度學習需要非常多樣本才能訓練模型，也就是需要大量資料來擬合模型。

cues.en: And why is that the case?
cues.zh: 為什麼會這樣？

cues.en: Why do we need so many examples, so much data to fit these deep learning models?
cues.zh: 為什麼需要那麼多範例、那麼多資料，才能擬合深度學習模型？

cues.en: Well, the answer comes from random sampling and sampling variability.
cues.zh: 答案來自隨機抽樣與抽樣變異。

cues.en: And you are going to learn in this video what this concept means.
cues.zh: 這支影片會介紹這個概念的意義。

cues.en: So to start with, let's think about a scientific question.
cues.zh: 先思考一個科學問題。

cues.en: How tall is the average Montenegrin?
cues.zh: 蒙特內哥羅人的平均身高是多少？

cues.en: A Montenegrin is a person who lives in the country Montenegro.
cues.zh: 蒙特內哥羅人，就是住在蒙特內哥羅這個國家的人。

cues.en: Now for this purpose, for you know, for this video, we don't actually care about the answer.
cues.zh: 以這支影片的目的而言，我們其實不在意答案。

cues.en: It doesn't matter how tall they actually are.
cues.zh: 他們實際有多高並不重要。

cues.en: Although I will give you the answer in a few slides.
cues.zh: 雖然再過幾張投影片，我還是會給你答案。

cues.en: The question is, how do we know the answer?
cues.zh: 問題是，我們怎麼知道答案？

cues.en: How do we find out the average height of a Montenegrin?
cues.zh: 要怎麼找出蒙特內哥羅人的平均身高？

cues.en: By the way, here is the country of Montenegro.
cues.zh: 順便說，這裡就是蒙特內哥羅。

cues.en: I've never been there, but from pictures on Google it seems to be a beautiful, beautiful country.
cues.zh: 我從沒去過，但看 Google 上的照片，似乎是非常、非常美麗的國家。

cues.en: Anyway, uh, so how tall is the average Montenegrin?
cues.zh: 總之，蒙特內哥羅人的平均身高是多少？

cues.en: Well, the way we can find this out is by going to Montenegro.
cues.zh: 可以親自去蒙特內哥羅找答案。

cues.en: And after a couple weeks of holiday and hiking and, you know, relaxing on the beach, then we get down to science, we go around, we just, you know, we find a big crowd of Montenegrins, and we just
cues.zh: 先度假幾個星期，健行、在海邊放鬆，然後再開始做科學；找到一大群蒙特內哥羅人，

cues.en: pick one person at random, like this guy, and then we take his height.
cues.zh: 隨機挑一個人，例如這位先生，再測量身高。

cues.en: We, you know, we bring a ruler with us, and we measure that guy and we find out that he has 160cm tall.
cues.zh: 帶著尺，量出他是一百六十公分。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: But that is just one person.
cues.zh: 但這只是一個人。

cues.en: We pick another random person and that person is taller.
cues.zh: 再隨機挑另一個人，那個人比較高。

cues.en: That person is 192cm tall.
cues.zh: 身高是一百九十二公分。

cues.en: It's pretty tall.
cues.zh: 相當高。

cues.en: But then, you know, we look up on Google, and the internet says that the average Montenegrin is or
cues.zh: 接著，上 Google 查一下，網路說蒙特內哥羅人的平均，

cues.en: the average height of Montenegrins is Two centimeters tall.
cues.zh: 身高是「兩公分」（原字幕數值缺漏，待核）。

cues.en: Now, if this is the average, why is it that we get one person who's shorter than the average and one person who's taller than the average?
cues.zh: 如果這是平均數，為什麼一個人比平均矮，另一個卻比平均高？

cues.en: Well, the obvious answer is sampling variability.
cues.zh: 很明顯，答案是抽樣變異。

cues.en: Not everyone has the same height.
cues.zh: 不是每個人的身高都相同。

cues.en: Just because there is an average height around this value.
cues.zh: 即使平均身高大約在這個值。

cues.en: So sampling variability refers to the phenomenon that different randomly selected samples from the same population can have different values of the same measurement.
cues.zh: 抽樣變異指的是，從同一個母體隨機選出的不同樣本，在相同測量上可能有不同數值。

cues.en: So we are measuring height with the same ruler in every person.
cues.zh: 我們對每個人，都用同一把尺量身高。

cues.en: It's the same.
cues.zh: 是一樣的。

cues.en: So the same measurement the same ruler.
cues.zh: 相同的測量，相同的尺。

cues.en: But we take different samples and we are going to get different values.
cues.zh: 但抽到不同樣本，就會得到不同數值。

cues.en: So this means that a single measurement is likely to be an unreliable estimate of a population parameter.
cues.zh: 所以，單次測量可能無法可靠估計母體參數。

cues.en: Now how reliable or unreliable a single measurement is depends on a variety of factors.
cues.zh: 單次測量究竟可靠或不可靠到什麼程度，取決於很多因素。

cues.en: Mainly, it depends on the variability of the distribution.
cues.zh: 主要取決於分布的變異程度。

cues.en: But this is important for deep learning because, you know, let's say we're building a model that can recognize cats, that can detect when a cat is in a picture.
cues.zh: 這對深度學習很重要。例如，假設要建立一個能辨識貓、偵測圖片裡是否有貓的模型。

cues.en: Well, if every single cat in the universe looked exactly the same, you know, in the way that every electron in the universe is exactly the same.
cues.zh: 如果宇宙裡每隻貓都長得完全相同，就像宇宙裡每個電子都一樣。

cues.en: If every single cat looked exactly the same, and every picture were taken from the same angle, we wouldn't actually need, you know, thousands of examples of pictures of cats.
cues.zh: 如果每隻貓都一模一樣，每張照片也都從相同角度拍攝，就不需要幾千張貓的圖片。

cues.en: We would only need one picture of a cat.
cues.zh: 只需要一張貓的圖片。

cues.en: But obviously that's not the case.
cues.zh: 但很明顯，現實不是如此。

cues.en: There are different kinds of cats.
cues.zh: 貓有不同種類。

cues.en: Cats look very different from each other.
cues.zh: 彼此的外觀差很多。

cues.en: We have some weird examples of cats here and corona safe cats.
cues.zh: 這裡有一些奇怪的貓，還有防疫安全的貓。

cues.en: So we need to collect a large sample of images of cats because of sampling variability.
cues.zh: 所以，因為抽樣變異，我們需要收集大量貓的影像。

cues.en: So where does sampling variability even come from?
cues.zh: 抽樣變異究竟從哪裡來？

cues.en: Why do we have variability in our samples?
cues.zh: 為什麼樣本會有變異？

cues.en: Well part of the answer is that there's natural variation.
cues.zh: 部分原因，是自然界本來就存在差異。

cues.en: This is often seen in biology and in physics, so there's just natural variation all over the place.
cues.zh: 生物學與物理學經常看到，自然變異無所不在。

cues.en: Part of it is measurement noise.
cues.zh: 部分則是測量雜訊。

cues.en: Our sensors are imperfect.
cues.zh: 我們的感測器並不完美。

cues.en: For example, you know, in the example I gave with the height of Montenegrins, we're just using a regular ruler.
cues.zh: 例如剛才蒙特內哥羅人身高的例子，只使用一般的尺。

cues.en: So we can say that it's accurate up to about a centimeter or maybe half a centimeter.
cues.zh: 可以說，精確到大約一公分，或半公分。

cues.en: But if we wanted to measure more precisely, let's say up to a nanometer, then, you know, our sensors are just not good enough.
cues.zh: 但如果要更精密，例如到一奈米，感測器就不夠好了。

cues.en: Our rulers are not good enough to get that level of precision.
cues.zh: 一般尺無法達到那種精度。

cues.en: So that alone introduces a little bit of noise and sampling variability.
cues.zh: 光這件事，就會帶來一些雜訊與抽樣變異。

cues.en: Also, complex systems have variables that depend on or interact with other variables.
cues.zh: 另外，複雜系統裡，有些變數會依賴其他變數，或與它們互相作用。

cues.en: So for example, if we were to measure height of lots of randomly selected people while ignoring age, the sampling variability would increase a lot, right?
cues.zh: 例如，隨機測量很多人的身高，卻忽略年齡，抽樣變異就會大幅增加，對吧？

cues.en: Because we are mixing together the height of babies with the height of adults.
cues.zh: 因為把嬰兒和成人的身高混在一起。

cues.en: And you know, the universe is just a random and wildly unpredictable place.
cues.zh: 而宇宙本來就是隨機，而且難以預測的地方。

cues.en: So there's just some natural stochasticity, I guess that's related to this first point I made here.
cues.zh: 所以，還有自然的隨機性；我想這和第一點有關。

cues.en: Okay, so what do we do about sampling variability?
cues.zh: 那要怎麼處理抽樣變異？

cues.en: Well, you know, the obvious solution is to take lots and lots of samples so that we can compute an average.
cues.zh: 很明顯的方法，是取得非常多樣本，計算平均數。

cues.en: And the idea is that the more variability there is, the more samples that we need to approximate the true population mean.
cues.zh: 概念是，變異越大，就需要越多樣本，才能近似真正的母體平均數。

cues.en: This is related to a concept in statistics called the law of large numbers.
cues.zh: 這和統計學裡的大數法則有關。

cues.en: Essentially this means that the larger samples we take, the more samples we take, the more data we collect, the better we are going to be able to estimate the true underlying statistics that we really
cues.zh: 基本上，樣本越大、樣本數越多、收集的資料越多，就越能準確估計我們真正，

cues.en: care about.
cues.zh: 關心的底層統計量。

cues.en: You will see examples of this also in deep learning throughout the rest of this course, that when we
cues.zh: 這門課接下來的深度學習範例，也會看到，如果，

cues.en: are working with relatively simple stimuli, relatively simple data values, we actually don't need that many samples.
cues.zh: 刺激或資料值相對簡單，其實不需要那麼多樣本。

cues.en: In fact, you'll see Sometimes we were.
cues.zh: 事實上，有時候我們會，

cues.en: We will be simulating our own data, we'll be generating our own data.
cues.zh: 自行模擬、自行產生資料。

cues.en: And we get really, really good deep learning model performance based on only 100 samples.
cues.zh: 只靠一百個樣本，就能讓深度學習模型有非常好的表現。

cues.en: But if you would try to train a much more complex, really deep convolutional neural network with 100 pictures, you're not going to get anywhere.
cues.zh: 但如果只用一百張圖片，去訓練非常複雜、很深的卷積神經網路，就不會有什麼成果。

cues.en: Okay, so have lots and lots of data.
cues.zh: 好的，所以要有大量資料。

cues.en: That's one thing that we need to overcome the issue of sampling variability.
cues.zh: 這是克服抽樣變異，需要具備的條件之一。

cues.en: So again why we need to worry about sampling variability in deep learning.
cues.zh: 再說一次，深度學習為什麼要在意抽樣變異？

cues.en: Well deep learning models learn by examples.
cues.zh: 因為模型是透過範例學習。

cues.en: So we need to have lots of examples for our deep learning models to actually learn effectively.
cues.zh: 所以，需要大量範例，才能有效學習。

cues.en: This is also an important issue because non-random or biased sampling can introduce systematic biases
cues.zh: 這也很重要，因為非隨機或有偏的抽樣，可能把系統性偏差，

cues.en: into the deep learning models, and prevent them from learning the way that we want them to learn.
cues.zh: 帶進模型，讓模型無法按照我們期待的方式學習。

cues.en: This is a topic I will discuss in more detail later in the course.
cues.zh: 之後會更詳細討論。

cues.en: We need to have random sampling in order for the models to be good.
cues.zh: 要讓模型表現好，需要隨機抽樣。

cues.en: If we don't have random samples, we have non-representative or biased sampling that can cause overfitting and it limits the generalizability.
cues.zh: 如果不是隨機樣本，而是缺乏代表性或有偏的抽樣，可能造成過度擬合，限制泛化能力。

cues.en: Again, this is a big term.
cues.zh: 同樣，這是個大主題。

cues.en: This is you know, there's a lot to unpack in this sentence here I'm going to talk more about this.
cues.zh: 這句話包含很多內容，之後會再多談。

cues.en: We're going to have several videos just on this topic later in the course.
cues.zh: 稍後會有幾支影片，專門討論這個主題。
